concerns.text: T018a mandates resampling 'ALL' datasets to 'hourly' frequency. Spec US1-AC3 only requires resampling the 'UK National Grid Load' dataset to a consistent frequency. Applying hourly resampling to NOAA (daily) and Yahoo (intraday/daily) data without spec authorization silently relaxes the data fidelity requirements and introduces unnecessary distortion, violating the principle that tasks must not silently relax what the spec demands.

T010 requires computing metrics for 'ALL shuffled versions' and lists dependencies on T019a/T019b (shuffling generation). However, T019a/b are defined in the same phase. This creates a circular dependency where T010 cannot run until shuffled files exist, but the generation tasks (T019a/b) are logically blocked by the need for metrics (T010) to define the output schema or validation criteria. This structural deadlock prevents the verification of FR-003 (shuffling) and US2-AC5 (null distribution) as defined in the spec.

T037a_impl implements linear regression but relies on a separate task (T037c) for VIF and N_eff calculation. FR-005 mandates that the regression model 'MUST calculate the Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) and Effective Sample Size (N_eff)'. Splitting this into a separate task risks the primary regression output (T037a_impl) being generated without these mandatory validation metrics if T037c is skipped or fails, effectively weakening the deliverable of the regression task.

T050 is marked as [ ] (unimplemented/pending) and requires inputs from T037b (filtered features) and T037 (Monte Carlo). However, T037a_runner (the execution task) lists T050 as a hard dependency. This creates a blocking deadlock where the regression cannot run because T050 is not yet implemented, yet T050 requires the completion of the very tasks it gates. This violates the requirement that tasks must be executable and not introduce silent deadlocks that prevent the fulfillment of FR-005.
